public_rationale: Ramp establishes concentrated spending within its sample. That does not establish that the largest spenders are all AI startups, that their token purchases require venture subsidies, or that the sample represents either provider's total revenue. The available records do not settle the asserted dependence.
limitations: A venture-backed company can fund purchases from sales, financing, or both.
Business spending concentration cannot be substituted for the financing composition of total revenue.

our_interpretation: The plain reading is substantial dependence by both providers on startup customers whose token purchases require continuing venture financing.
Held up means dependence material to maintaining revenue, not merely that some customers have venture investors.
The latest completed quarter before publication, July through September 2026, is the evaluation window for the current causal relationship; this is an evaluator choice.
The context relies on reported figures and sampled spending estimates, so the accounting basis is estimate.
criteria.support_condition: Representative customer revenue and funding records show that both providers materially depend on startup token purchases financed by venture capital rather than the startups' own customer receipts.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Comparable records show that venture-financed startup purchases are immaterial to maintaining either provider's revenue, or that the relevant startup purchases are substantially self-funded from customer receipts.
